scenes.recognized_speech: Build a solid from little unit cubes. From one angle you can see the front and the top, but some cubes are hidden. The layers give you a way to count every cube in the solid. Think of lifting one level at a time.

In AMC Upper Primary Practice, a picture might ask how many cubes make a shape. In a Rossmoyne -style spatial puzzle, the diagram may show holes or an opening. Sketch a plan of each layer so you can track which cubes stay.
This block is three cubes wide, too deep, and too high. How many unit cubes does it contain? Think about how many positions there are on just the bottom layer.
1 layer has 2 rows with 3 cubes in each row that gives 6 cubes, the upper layer has exactly the same 6 positions. Together there are 12 cubes including cubes the outside drawing hides.
a block has six stacks. Their heights front row first are 1, 3, 2, then 4, 1, 3. All stacks rest on the table. How many cubes are in the block? Try counting level by level from the table up.

Level 1 has 6 cubes, 4 of those stacks reach level 2, 3 stacks reach level 3, and 1 reaches level 4. Add 6, 4, 3, and 1 to get 14. Summing the 6 heights gives 14 as well. That is an independent check.

Start with a solid 4x4x3 block. Remove a vertical column of 3 cubes. Also remove a straight tunnel of 4 cubes across the middle layer. The tunnel passes through the same column. How many cubes remain?

Each of the three layers originally contained 16 cubes, removing the vertical column takes one from every layer, the tunnel runs through four positions on the middle layer. One of them is already empty, the tunnel takes only three more cubes.
Count what's left, the bottom and top each have 15 cubes. The middle has 12 because four of its 16 positions are empty. 15 plus 12 plus 15 is 42. As a check, 48 minus 6 is also 42.

A visible cube count misses the cubes inside. A second mistake is subtracting 3 and 4 when their paths meet. The shared cube can be removed once. Mark the empty cells by layer or subtract the shared cell from the removal count.

In an exam, identify the base dimensions and the number of levels, label hidden positions on a quick layer sketch, when two cuts cross, mark their common cell. Finally, check your counter second way, using full volume, minus the missing cubes.
